split.development: test/act-shell.test.mjs: 23 cases that existed before this item (one of them the failing case) plus 5 added by it; the fix was written against the failing case and the added cases
split.why: a behaviour test of process kills on one host, with no data to hold out: every case spawns real processes and asserts what the operating system reports

statement: On this Windows PC the shell hand that runs a command must kill the command and everything it started when its time is up, and say honestly that it did. Before this change the hand did kill the whole tree, but it wrote the kill down as if the program had finished on its own with exit code 1, so one of its tests failed. The fix records a kill it performed as a kill. The test file ran twice: 27 passed, 0 failed, 1 skipped of 28, then 27 passed, 0 failed, 1 skipped of 28. In the added case a grandchild process that detached itself was alive while the command ran and gone after the kill; in the control, where only the parent is killed the ordinary way, the same kind of grandchild was still alive and still writing, which is why the whole tree kill exists. With the fix switched off in memory the same tests showed 3 failures, so the bar can see the defect. There is no held-out data: this is a behaviour test of one machine, not a model.
